clinician.final_diagnosis: Pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma of the adult bladder
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old Chinese male presented with 10 days of intermittent gross hematuria. B ultrasound revealed hypoechoic nodules in the right upper bladder wall. Cystoscopy identified a 3.0 × 3.0 cm globular mass with a narrow pedicle and sheet-like yellow calcification on the right anterior bladder wall. Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBt) was performed. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma with supporting immunohistochemistry (MyoD1+, myogenin partial+, vimentin+, Ki67 45%+, P53 90%+, CK−, SMA−, GATA3−). Tumor biopsy showed no residual tumor in the bladder muscularis. Pre-chemotherapy PET-CT staging showed no metastatic lesions. The patient received postoperative chemotherapy with intravenous dacarbazine and doxorubicin with good tolerability and no adverse events. Enhanced CT on 4 June 2024 (approximately 11 months post-diagnosis) showed no tumor recurrence.
